_comment: Row 350. Eight exact-once regressions restore reusable capture and cancellation PIDs, split mass-import admission and recovery, erase run identity, or let competing terminal writers overwrite one another. The companion transform control applies the identical M7 numeric-PID transform to an import-only node and must ESCAPE.
subject: job lifecycle APIs report success only when identity-bound durable state agrees

mutants.label: M1 treat every live numeric capture PID as the recorded owner
mutants.old:
if (current["pid_start"] == recorded_start
                        and current["boot_id"] == recorded_boot):
                    return False
mutants.new:
if True:  # mutant: reusable PID regains authority
                    return False

mutants.label: M2 launch persists only the reusable capture PID
M3 release mass-import admission lock between count and insert
M4 first-use recovery uses a fresh lock for every caller
M5 recovery rewrites current-run jobs as crashed
M6 dev-run launch retains no pidfd identity
mutants.new: pidfd = None  # mutant: launch retains no identity handle

mutants.label: M7 dev cancellation signals the reusable numeric PID
M8 worker completion overwrites cancellation's terminal verdict
mutants.old:
if run["state"] == "running":
        run["state"] = "done" if returncode == 0 else "failed"
mutants.new:
if True:  # mutant: every finisher overwrites terminal state
        run["state"] = "done" if returncode == 0 else "failed"
